headline: U.S. IT Recruiter @PioneerConsultingServices | Hiring Java, Full Stack Developers, Software, AI Engineers, Data Engineers, Analysts, BAs, PMs | Entry-Level to Senior | USC • GC • EAD • OPT
text:
I thought I was good at SQL… until I faced real interview questions.

Most interviews don’t just test your syntax — they challenge how you think, solve problems, and handle complex scenarios.

Here are 20 real SQL interview questions that pushed me beyond just writing SELECT *:

1️⃣ How do you handle Slowly Changing Dimensions without stored procedures?
2️⃣ Can you clearly explain all JOIN types and when to prefer FULL OUTER JOIN?
3️⃣ How do you calculate cumulative percentages within a partition?
4️⃣ What’s your approach to spotting gaps in sequences (like missing IDs)?
5️⃣ How do you enforce data integrity without using foreign keys?
6️⃣ COALESCE vs ISNULL — when and why would you use either?
7️⃣ How do you compare two huge tables efficiently to find mismatched rows?
8️⃣ What’s the safest way to update millions of rows without locking production tables?
9️⃣ How would you aggregate hourly or daily data from timestamp values?
🔟 How do you generate dynamic SQL — without using stored procedures?

1️⃣1️⃣ Correlated vs non-correlated subqueries — what’s the difference and when to use which?
1️⃣2️⃣ How do you delete records older than a year from a massive table?
1️⃣3️⃣ What is a recursive CTE, and where is it most effective?
1️⃣4️⃣ How do you ensure ACID properties in a high-throughput OLTP environment?
1️⃣5️⃣ How do you store and query JSON efficiently in relational databases?
1️⃣6️⃣ How do indexes affect performance in write-heavy systems?
1️⃣7️⃣ What’s the real value of reading a query execution plan?
1️⃣8️⃣ How do you write a query to calculate year-over-year growth?
1️⃣9️⃣ What are window frames, and how do they differ in analytical functions?
2️⃣0️⃣ How would you design a schema for a real-time analytics dashboard?

⸻

These aren’t just interview questions—they’re your checklist to:
✅ Think deeply
✅ Write smarter SQL
✅ Design scalable, production-grade systems

This is a classic FAANG-level SQL question. Most candidates fail it by over-engineering. 💎

The best SQL solution isn't the longest one. It’s the most readable one.

You have a Club table where members earn rewards. The catch? Multiple rewards are stored as a colon-separated string (e.g., 'MM:CI:CD') in a single column.

✅ Using STRING_SPLIT to handle delimited data

author: Aditya Bansal
headline: 14K+ @LinkedIn | YouTuber ▶️ | SQL Champion 💥| Snowflake Data Engineer | DBT | SQL Server | SnowPro Core Certified | Mentor | Open to Collab
text:
Most Data Engineers can write SQL, but 80% fail this "Gaps & Islands" question at Deloitte. 🛑
Why? Because it’s not about syntax—it’s about mathematical logic. 🧠

📌 The Scenario:
You're given a list of event dates. Some are consecutive (a "streak"), and some have gaps. 

🎯Your task is simple:
Group the streaks and find the Start and End date for each.

❌The Trap:
Most candidates freeze when they realize a simple GROUP BY isn't enough. If the dates aren't exactly the same, how do you group them?

🧠The Secret: It’s called the Difference Method. 🛠️
By subtracting a row sequence from your dates, all consecutive dates "anchor" to the same constant value. It’s one of those elegant patterns that separates senior engineers from the rest.

💡I’ve seen this exact pattern show up in Big 4 interviews more than almost any other. If you can’t handle "islands" of data, you'll struggle with real-world time-series analysis.

headline: Sr. Data Engineer at Accenture Strategy |Ex-Deloitte, PwC | 3x Azure, 2x Databricks Certified | Transforming Data into Insights for Impact
text:
If you’re preparing for a 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲, 𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗱𝘂𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝗦𝗤L is an important interview Question

Duplicate data is not just a data quality issue — it’s a system reliability problem.

𝗜𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗽𝗶𝗽𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀, 𝗱𝘂𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝘀𝗻𝗲𝗮𝗸 𝗶𝗻 𝗱𝘂𝗲 𝘁𝗼:

 • Multiple source systems
 • Retry mechanisms
 • Late-arriving data
 • API reprocessing
 • Streaming replays

If not handled properly, duplicates can silently break analytics, reporting, and downstream systems.

🔹 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗱𝘂𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗿𝗼𝘂𝘀

❌ Inflated metrics (revenue, counts, KPIs)
❌ Incorrect dashboards & business decisions
❌ Data inconsistency across layers
❌ Failed joins and unexpected results
❌ Performance degradation at scale

🔹 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗿’𝘀 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗱𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗲

SQL gives you powerful tools to detect, prevent, and eliminate duplicates, such as:

✔ ROW_NUMBER() for deduplication logic
✔ DISTINCT (used carefully)
✔ GROUP BY with aggregation
✔ Primary keys & constraints
✔ Incremental loads with watermarking
✔ MERGE logic for upserts

🔹 Real-world example

Imagine a daily sales pipeline that accidentally loads the same file twice.
Without deduplication:

Revenue doubles
Reports become unreliable
Trust in data breaks
With proper SQL dedup logic:
Data stays accurate
Pipelines remain idempotent
Systems scale safely

🔑 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆

For Data Engineers, handling duplicates isn’t optional — it’s mandatory.

Clean data pipelines are built on:
✔ Idempotent design
✔ Strong #SQL logic
✔ Thoughtful data modeling

text:
🔥 THIS SQL QUESTION IS SILENTLY FAILING 80% OF CANDIDATES 🔥
I solved the “Highest Cost Orders” problem today — and it perfectly exposes how interviews actually test SQL 👇
❌ It’s NOT about writing SELECT *
 ❌ It’s NOT about memorizing syntax
✅ It’s about:
Thinking in daily aggregations
Handling multiple orders per day
Ranking within a date, not globally
Returning ALL ties (this is where most people fail 👀)
📌 The trick?

SUM() + RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY order_date)
This single pattern shows up in:
Data Engineer interviews
Analytics roles
Real production ETL logic
If you can explain WHY PARTITION BY matters here — you’re already ahead of most candidates.
